NKE.rationale: NKE is a structurally deteriorating business trading at a premium valuation with no near-term fundamental catalyst to reverse the trajectory. Revenue is flat YoY (+0.1%) but declining sequentially (-9.2% QoQ). The critical issue is a severe margin recession: operating margin has collapsed to 5.8% (from 7.5% YoY and 8.0% QoQ), net margin has fallen to 4.8% (from 9.4% a year ago), and EPS diluted is down -35.2% YoY to $0.35. Cash generation has deteriorated in lockstep, with operating cash flow down -76% YoY to $430M. Despite this fundamental collapse, the stock trades at 31.2x diluted earnings — a 54% premium to the 20.2x P/E of a year ago when profitability was nearly double. The earnings yield of 3.2% offers no margin of safety versus the 4.45% 10-year Treasury yield. Market share is declining for a third consecutive year (global athletic footwear share fell to 22.9% in 2025, losing ~3 percentage points YoY), with competitors On Running and Hoka gaining ground. Management has pushed the growth-recovery timeline to Q2 FY2027, and short interest has surged from 0.41% to 4.67% of float. The balance sheet is a partial offset (net-cash position with $8.06B cash vs $8.03B debt, 24-year dividend streak), but this cushion is insufficient to offset the combination of deteriorating fundamentals, elevated valuation, and absence of a near-term catalyst. The Q4 FY2026 report (June 30) is the next data point but is unlikely to show a margin inflection given the structural headwinds. All three pillars — fundamental deterioration, rich valuation vs own history, and no credible near-term catalyst — are aligned negatively.

Earnings yield of 3.2% well below 10-year Treasury yield of 4.45% (2026-05-28), implying no margin of safety
